properties.Name: East Liberty
properties.Description: An at-the-time bustling black business district in Pittsburgh, but suffered from the same Urban Renewal practices the Hill District did. When the Lower Hill was leveled for the construction of the Civic Arena, this was a place it's residents moved.

properties.Name: HOLC D-10
properties.Description: The Home Owners' Loan Corporation established this area as D-grade, covering almost the entire Hill District. The intended purpose was to help banks assess mortgage risk, but in application, it reflects the racial bias of those who designated it so. This is what Redlining is: it's a way to deny black people mortgages, and tell developers "this land is unvaluable, and a blank canvas."

properties.Name: HOLC D-8
properties.Description: This redline area cuts straight through the heart of East Liberty, and essentially marked it for eventual death. It also covers the southern half of Homewood's neighborhoods

properties.Name: Bedford Dwellings
properties.Date: Completed in the 40s, expanded in the 50s

properties.Name: Lower Hill
properties.Description: The part of the Hill closest to Downtown Pittsburgh, a once-bustling neighborhood. When it was partially demolished for the Civic Arena, around 8,000 residents lost their homes, and 400 black & minority owned businesses were destroyed.
